name: Aspect & Fall
oneLiner: A garden and landscape design studio whose page is the drawing set itself — what a space becomes, month by month and year by year.
paletteSeed: drafting paper (warm off-white), graphite (a warm near-black, never pure) and non-photo blue for the setting-out grid — the drafting-pencil blue that deliberately does not reproduce; the ONE colour rule is that the only saturated colour on the page belongs to PLANTS and changes with the month, so nothing decorative is ever coloured — honest to a discipline where the colour on a plan IS the planting
typeDirection: Spectral (roman + italic — the italic carries the Latin binomials as horticultural print has always set them) + Sometype Mono (every piece of sheet apparatus: title block, labels, dimensions, readouts) — TWO families only, because a real drawing sheet has exactly two lettering registers; both OFL, vendored, both portfolio-new
motionBudget: one scroll clock and no second animation system: the calendar year runs Jan→Dec across a pinned drawing sheet, and one clock sets the coloured-pencil fill in the beds, which species are lit in their own colour, the terrace's shade polygon as the canopy leafs, three live readouts, the playhead crossing the interest calendar, and how far the PHOTOGRAPH has moved through its own year — three generated transitions (Feb→May→Jul→Oct) of one locked-off corner, decoded to frame sequences and scrubbed by scroll position rather than played, because seeking a compressed video lands on keyframes and janks; the photograph LEADS the sheet and the plan proves it, never a picture appended to a diagram and never a diagram ranked above the thing it describes; the maturity chapter (year 1/3/10) is three static states, not a second clock; reduced-motion and no-JS both get the single static July frame and never build the sequence at all, with every chapter, the full calendar and the wink's line still in the markup; THE WINK lands at high summer only — a leader line on the plan pointing at the sunny end of the terrace, annotated 'CAT SITS HERE', the kind of dry margin note a real designer actually pencils in

verdict.note: Site B of the landing arc (docs/landing-arc/spec.md). Built with site A's three ratchets applied from the opener: the SCHEMATIC test rejected the banked naturalistic 'one tree through four seasons' outright and moved the instrument to the drawing the discipline actually produces — a plan-view planting plan with canopy circles at mature spread, plus a seasonal interest calendar. s106 VIDEO PASS: the stage was REBALANCED on founder direction (a top-down plan does not show what the season does) — the photograph now leads at 63% of the instrument area where it held 24%, and it MOVES: three generated Seedance transitions scrubbed by scroll. Building the scrub exposed a defect the cross-fade had been hiding — the shipped October keyframe was a different camera, measured 24px+ out of register against the other three — so it was re-minted registered to July and the /guide now records it.
